# Scans: point clouds, meshes, reverse engineering, inspection

A scan is a point cloud (XYZ/ASC/CSV/PTS text, PLY, PCD, E57 — E57 in metres becomes mm, each scan posed) or a mesh (STL, OBJ, PLY, glTF/GLB, 3MF) added to the project with `./ise scan add <file> [--source colmap|object-capture|scanner]`; the reply gives its id (a content hash, like imported files). Photogrammetry plugs in here: COLMAP's fused PLY or Apple Object Capture's OBJ/PLY are just scans with a `--source`. Every operation below makes a new scan (its `parent` is the one it came from), so nothing is lost. The person has the same in the Scans tool (the scan icon on the rail): add, check with markers on the problems, repair, rework, fit, make a part, and inspect with a colour map.

- Check and repair a mesh: `./ise mesh check <scan>` counts holes, open and non-manifold edges and vertices, flipped, degenerate, duplicate and crossing triangles, pieces, and says where. `./ise mesh repair <scan> [--no-fill] [--max-edges N] [--largest] [--min-component 0.05]` welds, drops duplicate and degenerate triangles, untangles non-manifold edges and vertices, cuts out crossing triangles, makes normals agree and point out, fills holes with refined, faired patches (Liepa), and reports each step with counts before and after. Also `mesh fill-holes | harmonize | flip | largest | split | merge <scan> <other…>`, `mesh trim <scan> --origin x,y,z --normal nx,ny,nz` (keeps what is behind the plane, cut open).
- Rework: `mesh decimate <scan> --ratio 0.25 | --triangles N [--max-error mm]` (quadric edge collapse; reports how far it strays), `mesh smooth [--iterations 10] [--laplacian]` (Taubin keeps volume; Laplacian shrinks), `mesh remesh --edge 2` (even triangles, sharp edges kept), `mesh sample --count N` (mesh → points). Points: `scan downsample --voxel 1 | --count N`, `scan outliers [--neighbours 16 --sigma 2]`, `scan normals [--toward x,y,z]`, `scan crop <scan> --box … | --near … --within …`, `scan merge <scan> <other…>`.
- Surfaces from points: `scan reconstruct <scan> [--depth 7] [--trim 2.5]` (Poisson; closed unless trimmed back where there are no points; reports how closely it passes the points). In programs `reconstruct(sha, { depth })` is a closed solid.
- Read intent back (reverse engineering — then build exact geometry from the numbers, never ship the scan as the part): `scan fit <scan> [auto|plane|sphere|cylinder|cone|torus] [--near x,y,z --within r | --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1] [--ransac --threshold mm]` gives the primitive's parameters and RMS/worst error (fits are robust to a few stray points); `scan detect <scan> [--kinds plane,cylinder] [--threshold mm]` finds every primitive, largest first. In programs: `const c = fitScan(sha, "cylinder", { near: [30, 20, 17], within: 9 })` → `{ kind, base, axis, radius, length, rms, … }` (plane `{ point, normal }`, sphere `{ center, radius }`, cone `{ apex, axis, half_angle, half_angle_degrees, base, radius, length }`, torus `{ center, axis, major, minor }`), then `cylinder(c.length, c.radius)` placed with `placeOn(…, { at: c.base, normal: c.axis })` — exact in STEP, and it follows the scan if the scan is replaced. `detectShapes(sha)` lists them all. Free-form skins: `fitSurface(sha, { poles: 8 | [nu, nv], degree: 3, thickness: 1.5, box | near+within })` is an exact B-spline face thickened into a solid (STEP carries the true surface); `./ise scan surface <scan>` and `fitSurfaceInfo(sha, …)` give its numbers. `fitCurve(points | sha, { poles })` smooths ordered points into `{ samples }` for `spline(samples)`.
- Sections and curves: `mesh section <scan> --origin x,y,z --normal nx,ny,nz | --normal 0,0,1 --count 10` (loops with length and area); in programs `scanSection(sha, { origin, normal })` → loops with `flat` 2D points: `polygon(loop.flat).extrude(5)` placed with `placeOn(…, { at: s.origin, normal: s.normal, x: s.u })` rebuilds a profile from a scan. `mesh curvature <scan>` (mean, Gaussian, principal; 1/mm), `mesh segment <scan> [--angle 25] [--planes]` (regions with the primitive each fits best), `mesh boundaries <scan>` (open-edge loops), `mesh project <scan> '[[x,y,z],…]' [--step 1]` (a polyline laid onto the surface; in programs `curveOnScan(sha, points, { step })`).
- Flatten a skin: `mesh unwrap <scan> [--box … | --near … --within … | --segment N] [--sketch --name N] [--svg f.svg]` — least-squares conformal unwrap scaled to true area; reports area and length stretch; `--sketch` makes its outline a sketch to cut from.
- Mesh controls on any part: `mesh from <part> --tolerance 0.01 --angle 10 [--max-edge 2]` keeps the tessellation as a scan (to check, compare, export with `scan export`).
- Meshes in programs: `importMesh(sha, { repair: true, remesh: 2, decimate: 0.5, smooth: 3, refine: true })` (refine merges coplanar triangles into true flat faces in STEP — a mesh-made box exports as six planes); `scanMesh(sha, { repair: true })` for a scan's whole mesh; any solid has `.decimate(0.25 | n)`, `.smooth({ iterations })`, `.remesh(edge)`, `.refine()`. Mesh booleans are the ordinary `add/subtract/intersect` on these solids.
- Inspection: `./ise inspect <scan> <part> --tolerance 0.1 [--align icp|best] [--required 0.99] [--part P] [--require]` — every point's signed deviation from the part's surface (+ material where there should be none, − missing), min/max/mean/RMS/σ, the share within ±tolerance, the worst places, a histogram, PASS/FAIL; `--at x,y,z` adds the deviation at the scan point nearest that spot. `--align best` best-fits the scan first (principal axes, then point-to-plane ICP) and reports RMS before/after; use it for any scan not taken in the part's coordinates. `--require` adds the requirement `{ kind: "scan_deviation", part, scan, tolerance, within?, align? }`, which the engine re-checks on every change of the part like any other requirement.

### Photogrammetry: photos from many angles → a scan → a clean part

When the person has an object and a camera (or photos already), make the model from photos:

1. `./ise scan markers [--letter] [--out sheet.pdf]` — the marker sheet: six 30 mm coded markers round a 250 × 170 mm field. Ask them to print it at 100 % (the 100 mm bar must measure 100 mm), lay it flat and stand the object in the middle. An object longer than the field is fine (up to about 380 × 300 mm round the sheet's centre is kept whole) as long as most markers stay visible.
2. Capture: 30–80 sharp photos in two or three rings (low, ~30° and ~60° up), each overlapping the next by two thirds, markers in every photo, soft light that does not move, no zoom changes, original files (not edited, cropped or sent through a chat app). Portrait and landscape shots, or two phones, may be mixed (each photo size gets its own lens), and wide phone lenses are fine. Shiny, clear or plain parts need texture (scanning spray, chalk, tape): a glossy painted stapler came out about twice as rough as a matt carved one. iPhone photos with depth make Object Capture's size metric even without the sheet.
3. `./ise scan photos <folder | photos.zip | photo …> [--engine auto|object-capture|colmap] [--detail preview|reduced|medium|full] [--mask] [--name N]` — uploads the photos (JPG, PNG, HEIC) as a photo set and runs the engine as a background job (progress printed; `--detach` returns at once; `scan jobs`, `scan cancel <job>`). `scan engines` says which engines run here and what is missing: Apple Object Capture (macOS, Apple silicon; dense textured mesh; with the sheet in the photos it solves the cameras first and then models only the box over the sheet, so the object gets the mesh's triangles) and COLMAP (BSD; structure from motion, then dense stereo — with CUDA COLMAP's own, without it Iṣẹ́ Studio's dense matching on the CPU, about 1–4 minutes for 50 photos at `medium`; `full` matches larger photos, slower). It prints and keeps two scans: the engine's result, sized and levelled, and `<name> (clean)`: the floor cut away, what stands in the field kept whole (also where it reaches past the field, and loose parts that rise from it), things standing beside it and scraps of the floor dropped, holes filled, ≤ 200 000 triangles. Photos that walk through a room, a street or a façade instead of going round one object are kept whole (`not cleaned: a scene`); cut out the part wanted with `scan crop <scan> --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1`. The reply's quality says how many photos were used or rejected, reprojection error, the scale method and its uncertainty, coverage per 30° sector and elevation range, open holes, and advice (gaps to fill with more photos). `./ise scan quality <scan>` prints it again with the camera poses.
4. Size: with the sheet in the photos the scan is in millimetres, the sheet is the floor (z = 0) and its centre the origin (method `markers`, typically ±0.05 %). Without it (method `none`), measure a distance on the object and give two points of it on the scan: `./ise scan scale <scan> --from x,y,z --to x,y,z --distance mm [--pick mm]` (uncertainty from how precisely the points are picked: use plane or cylinder fits — `scan fit` — to place them, not single points); `scan level <scan>` puts a floor plane at z = 0. Say which method and uncertainty you used.
5. Into CAD: `mesh check` the clean scan, read the intent back with `scan fit`/`scan detect`/`fitSurface`, build a clean parametric part from the numbers (never ship the scan as the part), then `./ise inspect <clean scan> <part> --tolerance 0.3 --align best` and report RMS and the worst places. Deep pockets, tunnels and undersides the photos could not see come out filled or missing: the inspection shows them as large + or −; say so rather than chasing them.

What to expect (measured against true geometry: DTU's real photos with structured-light scans, and photo-real renders of photo-scanned objects on the printed sheet, 48 photos of 2400 × 1600 px at about 0.5 m, both engines): with the sheet the size is right to ±0.05–0.06 % and the scan sits within a few tenths of a millimetre of where it belongs; a matt, textured object of about 100 mm comes out within about 0.8–1.0 mm RMS of its true surface (95 % within about 1.2–1.5 mm, 87–92 % within ±0.5 mm after `--align best`), real photos about 0.4–0.8 mm mean error; a glossy or plain part (a painted metal stapler) about twice as rough and with gaps, unless sprayed; undersides and pockets the photos did not see are guessed (filled), off by several millimetres. So tell the person: overall shape to about ±1 mm and size to about 0.1 %; for fits finer than ±0.5 mm, measure those features (calipers) and build them from the numbers, using the scan for the shape round them.

Look at the photos before running an engine. A handful of separate views (front, top, side, three-quarter product shots on white, often retouched or sent through a chat app) cannot be aligned by either engine; say so and model the object from them as reference pictures instead, following **Model from reference photos** above (each view a calibrated canvas, the body from the views, the real features from the photos, every view compared until it matches). If an engine fails with "could not be placed relative to each other", that is this case.

To try the pipeline on a known shape, `./ise scan render-photos <folder> [--count 40] [--rings 25,50] [--distance mm] [--sheet]` draws the model from many angles (speckled like a part sprayed for scanning, on the marker sheet) and writes the true cameras to `cameras.json`.
